en: Fine cuts?
I've different cuts of meat from mutated and non-mutated animals. There's options for every budget. Even Vultures gotta eat, right?
I also have some jobs for you if you can't trade right now.
Organizing?
Indeed! Organizing is the way to go, my brother. How else do we survive this wasteland? How else do we defeat the Mist?
Can't do that shit alone! We must all lock arms, collectivize our work and reap the benefits! That's the way of the Rada!
Not sure I'm interested.

I've heard Vultures like to do things alone – I'm not knocking your hustle, but please reconsider that philosophy! Even pre-War history shows the power we have as a group, to solve issues, to increase production, to eradicate scarcity. Even in these dire conditions!
Do not cling to this image of a self-made survivalist; it is a fabrication, brother, as you rely on traders and clients to make a living.
I'd like to know more about organizing.
An important first step, my brother. Granted, it's not the simplest process for those used to putting themselves before others. But we can teach you to think differently.
We can teach you about community. We can infuse your blood with the future of Zalesye!
Changed my mind – tell me more about the Rada.
Is that so? Well, I'm glad you have some interest!
Tell me more about organizing with the Rada.
You think the Rada should lead Zalesye?
Yes. Compared to other factions, we are the best choice. Do you disagree?
Not convinced on you leading Zalesye.
I see. And what is the best alternative, in your opinion?
Got to get going, now.
How does organizing with the Rada work?

Organizing means working in tandem with many others so as to lighten the overall load. In our precarious situation, basic subsistence is the goal: supplying food, water, warmth and security to as many people as we can.
You'd be helping with security, mostly. We can always use a Vulture's firepower and expertise in traversing Zalesye. You'd also help us bring more people in, of course.

Meanwhile, we can educate, clothe and even feed you. Seems you don't need a spot in our bunkers that much, but maybe in an emergency? This type of thing is never set in stone, my brother. You have to live it to live it.
Are there any Vultures in the Rada?
I haven't seen a scavenger go through recruitment even once – they all flee the responsibility.
If I sound harsh, it's only to warn you that this is not a light decision – organizing is about commitment.
Any infighting among you?
Well, of course. We're trying to structurally and fundamentally change society – not really a way to do that without some disagreements!
But it's nothing you need to worry about beforehand. You'd have to be in the group to know and care about these disputes. Externally? We're all in unison.
What are the day-to-day activities?
Some tasks involve spreading the word, others involve your own specialty – scavenging, handling firearms, protecting each other from all sorts of threats; things you can teach.

But you're also supposed to learn. We study books from before the War and try to adapt them to our crazy world of today. We have lectures and discussion groups to try and set a blueprint for how to move forward – everyone contributes.
Oh, have you met Mila? She's one of our best teachers. You'll love her.
About something else...
I have to leave.
You've shown interest, but have you ever shown commitment?
And if even these basics disinterest you, I'm afraid we'll be occasional business partners and not much else.
Palatines and Gunners might be better; they have power.
It's true that firepower is important. Not only to protect us from Mutants and Bandits, but to guarantee our way of living.
Imagine restructuring Zalesye around community and collective thinking, only for a bunch of souped-up killers to come in from the RO-29 and dominate us through sheer force.

But you need more than that for lasting change, my brother. Commonfolk are the ones who feel each and every change before everybody else – they're most exposed. Whoever leads our society has to interact with them, and truly represent their interests.
Palatines don't do that; it's their weakness. And Gunners? HA! They only see the weak as people to exploit. We need <u>less</u> of that, not more.
Mechanists and Acolytes could lead through knowledge.

Matters of mind and spirit are necessary for human development, and can make our lives better. But that is not a given. Technology can be distorted to attenuate exploitation, and religion has all throughout history been co-opted by the ruling classes as a means of dominating and dulling the senses of the Commonfolk, like alcohol to an addict.

A specialist's proficiency in these subjects is not enough to lead a people, my brother. We need a comprehensive view of the whole picture – how all this relates to the structures of power imbued in society, which need to be destroyed and rebuilt with Commonfolk on top.

Otherwise, we overestimate the importance of one single thing – firepower, technology, religion — and then we get fascism, technocracy, theocracy. A perpetuation of our cycle of self-destruction, with few on top and the rest in misery.
Mudlarks and Vultures – only ones who can use the Mist...

...What on Earth are you talking about, my brother? Granted, you and those Mudlarks – you do know the Mist like no other. That is knowledge which us Rada are lacking. But the Mist is a killer, brother, nothing else. "Knowing" it is like a fly "knowing" pesticide.

In a time of strife, of desperate survival, you and the Mudlarks would see us bend the knee to world-ending powers? To some gas-shaped god which brought us the apocalypse? Is the end of suffering through death the only thing we can hope for? I refuse to believe this.
